# 01 Setup your environment

Run the common setup script and synchronize the local project with
GitHub.

```{r}
# Run the setup script containing package restoration, helper functions, etc.
source(here::here("scripts", "01-setup.R"))

# Pull changes from the online repository into this local project folder.
# This is especially important when collaborating on the same project.
system2("git", c("-C", here::here(), "pull"))

# show which package namespaces are loaded to memory with library()
search()

# authenticate your @student.rug.nl google account
gsheets_auth()
```

# 02 Read and reshape the data

In this script we will work with a vegetation dataset that is in wide format, where each species is a separate column. We will reshape the data into long format, where species is a single variable, and then plot the results.
The input vegetation database can optionally be opened in your browser to inspect it directly.
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WIzkUvunLk1buybZ04Oko8wnF65EbuXjWEviWbeAwu4

We will now reshape the data using piping from wide to long format, where
'speciesname' will become a single variable instead of distributed over multiple
columns; treat bare, litter, and moss will be treated as if they are species (see the
"data import cheatsheet"). We remove `Salicornia.europaea` and
`Salicornia.procumbens` from the dataset, as `Salicornia.sp` is their
sum of these two; the two species were not separated in earlier years
We will also remove the variables `bare`, `litter`, `mosses` as they are not really species

Now we want to find which species are most common in the dataset. Add a variable to the
dataset that is the rank number of the species according to summed
abundance of each species over the whole dataset (1 = most abundant
species).

```{r}
# add the rank variable


# Now merge with the long file, adding a new column that indicates the rank of the species for every observation. This we can use to filter the data for the more common species. 

FactVegCov_long |> 
  dplyr::left_join(FactVegCov_ranked, by = "speciesname") -> FactVegCov_long_ranked
print(FactVegCov_long_ranked)
```
